solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dog exhibition receives notice

indicators.note: an exhibition that receives something takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an exhibition is a show
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A dog show takes in a public announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a noun naming the show's entrants, but it is a verb: to dog someone is to follow them closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog and to shadow both mean to follow someone closely and secretly, verb synonyms.

clue.text: Feign upset at 9

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: 9 refers to the answer at 9 across, a breakfast cereal

explanation.surface: Pretend to be upset by the breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign and to simulate both mean to pretend or fake a feeling or condition.

clue.text: Middling two notes are the same

parts.note: A and D are two notes of the musical scale
A and D are two notes of the musical scale
things that equate are equal or the same

explanation.surface: In a so-so piece of music, two notes sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means merely satisfactory, so-so or middling rather than good.

clue.text: Just downplay regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Merely understate things on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only are adverbs meaning merely or no more than.

clue.text: Bent coppers replace team leader in position

indicators.note: coppers replace the leader, meaning one letter swaps in for the first letter of team

parts.note: a position on a question is an attitude

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of the word team
coppers are pennies, abbreviated p in British money

explanation.surface: Corrupt police officers take over from the team's boss in a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent coppers' reads as corrupt police, but 'Bent' is the definition (a natural talent) and coppers are pennies, P. The P replaces the first T of ATTITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent for something is a natural flair or talent for it, a synonym of a natural ability.

clue.text: No backsliding after I support advance text laying down the law

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that supports another sits beneath it
after places the last piece at the end

parts.note: a prescript is a text laid down in advance, an ordinance

indicators.note: sliding back means the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: No relapse after I back an earlier text that sets out legal rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescription is the act of laying down rules authoritatively, of dictating what must be done.

clue.text: Ideologically disheartened without thinking

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the whole middle, of the word is taken out

explanation.surface: A dejected ideologue acting mindlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the long middle EOLOGICAL from IDEOLOGICALLY, leaving the two letters at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something idly means doing it casually, with no purpose or thought.

clue.text: Well-informed director swallowed an account of the latest developments

definitions.text: an account of the latest developments

parts.note: to be up on a subject is to be well informed about it
ate means swallowed food

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable film boss took in a report on recent events.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is a report bringing someone up to date on what has happened.

clue.text: Last stop before adventure ends

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: to end is to stop

indicators.note: the ends of the word adventure are its closing letters

explanation.surface: The final halt before the adventure is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb: to last is to carry on. 'ends' takes the closing three letters URE of adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: To last and to endure both mean to continue or survive over time, verb synonyms.

clue.text: Minced mule is eaten at breakfast

indicators.note: minced food is chopped up, so these letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Chopped mule meat makes a breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit commonly served as a morning meal.

clue.text: Private society avoided getting caught inside

indicators.note: getting caught inside means the letter for caught goes into the other word

parts.note: to have eluded something is to have avoided it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A secret club dodged capture.
explanation.definitionFit: Private and secluded both describe a place sheltered from other people, adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Terrible toothache when consuming most of cold drink

indicators.note: a terrible state is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder
most of the word means all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Severe tooth pain while gulping a chilled beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when consuming' joins TOOTHACHE to COL (cold less its D), and all twelve letters are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate is a warm beverage made with cocoa and milk.

clue.text: Jeer at beheaded hooligan

indicators.note: a word that is beheaded loses its first letter

parts.note: to flout is to jeer at or scorn

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a thug who has been decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: FLOUT less its head letter F leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is a rough, uncouth young man, close in sense to a hooligan or yob.

clue.text: Power held by bailiff or censor

indicators.note: the answer is held within the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Authority is wielded by a bailiff or a censor.
explanation.definitionFit: Force and power are synonyms for strength or might that can be exerted.

clue.text: Main attraction may be a dwarf or a giant

definitions.meaning: the leading performer who draws the crowds

definitions.text: may be a dwarf or a giant
definitions.meaning: astronomers class suns as white dwarfs, red giants and so on

explanation.surface: The headline act could be a very small or very large person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dwarf or a giant' sounds like people of unusual size, but these are classes of celestial body, as in a white dwarf or red giant.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is both the headline performer of a show and a sun, which astronomers call dwarfs or giants.

clue.text: Bloomer reportedly also made from this

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a bloomer is something that blooms, a flower

explanation.surface: Word is that the loaf called a bloomer is made from this as well.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is also a British loaf of bread, which is why 'also made from this' works: the loaf is made from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flour is the milled grain from which bread loaves such as a bloomer are baked.

clue.text: Old savings account turned up something of value

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a TESSA was a Tax-Exempt Special Savings Account, a former British savings scheme

explanation.surface: An old savings account surfaced, turning out to be valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: TESSA was a tax-free British savings account of the 1990s, later replaced by the ISA.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is any item or resource that has worth to its owner.

clue.text: Liberal police state unfortunately leaves you completely in the dark

definitions.text: leaves you completely in the dark

indicators.note: something that turns out unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters go awry

explanation.surface: An oppressive regime run by police is, sadly, keeping people uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves you completely in the dark' reads like being kept uninformed, but it is literal: the Moon blocking the Sun entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: When the Moon wholly covers the Sun, daylight vanishes and observers are plunged into darkness.

clue.text: Fathom rules about the French perfect

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fathom, a unit of depth

indicators.note: rules about another piece means that piece sits inside them

parts.note: laws are rules
les is the French plural form of the

explanation.surface: Understand the regulations concerning the French, which are faultless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fathom' looks like a verb meaning understand, but it is the unit of depth, abbreviated F.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless means without a single defect, which is to say perfect.

clue.text: Third world ailment turns out to be fatal

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned around and laid out anew
the third letter of the word world

explanation.surface: A disease of the developing world proves deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third world' reads as one phrase, but 'Third' takes R, the third letter of world, to add to AILMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal illness is one that will end in death, so it is fatal.

clue.text: Unexpectedly excluded from the honour of representing Oxford or Cambridge

definitions.text: excluded from the honour of representing Oxford or Cambridge
definitions.meaning: a Blue is awarded to those who compete for Oxford or Cambridge University, so someone left out is not among them

explanation.surface: Surprisingly, someone was not picked for the university team.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is the sporting honour given to students who represent Oxford or Cambridge against each other; read literally, the phrase means being outside that group.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something arriving suddenly, like a bolt from a clear sky.

clue.text: Preserved sausage meat initially approved

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: OK'd, written OKED, means approved

explanation.surface: The cured banger had its meat given the go-ahead first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S and M from sausage meat; OK'd is approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been smoked has been cured over wood smoke to keep it from spoiling.

clue.text: Bother about Tory elected on the opposite side

indicators.note: a word that goes about others surrounds them

parts.note: a fag is British slang for a tiresome chore, a bother
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: Trouble surrounds a Conservative who has won his seat across the way.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is British slang for a wearisome task, as in 'what a fag'.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing means positioned opposite, looking towards something from the far side.

clue.text: Common purpose

definitions.meaning: low, vulgar or shabby in character
as a verb, to purpose is to intend

explanation.definitionFit: Mean as an adjective is low or common; as a verb it is to intend or purpose something.

clue.text: Party reject man as a benefactor

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the name is turned around

parts.note: Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A political party turns down a man as its patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, but it is a social do; 'reject' reverses RON to give NOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods to a cause, as a benefactor or patron does.

clue.text: Introduces sturdy walkway into marshland — the alternative is to sink

indicators.note: the introductions of words are their opening letters, taken from the next four words

explanation.surface: A firm boardwalk is laid across a bog, since otherwise you go under.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'sink or swim'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the saying sink or swim, the only alternative to going under is to keep afloat.

clue.text: Has to pay nothing over stitch up

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to sew is to stitch

explanation.surface: Someone must pay out nothing after a set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stitch up' looks like a frame-up, but 'up' reverses SEW to WES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owes money is in debt and so is obliged to pay it.

clue.text: Response from Brussels?

parts.note: a response coming back; the question mark points to EC, the European Community based in Brussels, at its start

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'response'; 'from Brussels?' hints at the EC, the European Community headquartered in Brussels, which begins the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound sent back, a response or reply.

clue.text: A winter king dressed in warm clothing

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: dressed, as in a dressed salad, means prepared or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch wrapped up against the cold in wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear covers jumpers, cardigans and other knitted garments worn for warmth.

clue.text: Score ten without occupational therapy test

indicators.note: without means the named letters are left out

explanation.surface: Getting ten points without any occupational therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: SCORE TEN loses its O and T, scattered in that order, to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen people is to test them for a disease or check their suitability.

clue.text: Taken in by a princess, a Greek goddess, a saint and a small boy

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, Princess of Wales
Ge, or Gaia, is the Greek goddess of the earth
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone was fooled by a royal, a deity, a holy figure and a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' looks like 'deceived', but it means absorbed, as food or information is.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or information that has been absorbed and assimilated has been digested.

clue.text: A bit further south within Luxembourg

indicators.note: the letter for south goes within the word for further

parts.note: more means further or additional
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A little further down inside the small European state.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small piece or bite of food, a bit.
